item.research_question: How can multi-elemental alloy nanoparticles (MEA-NPs) composed of traditionally immiscible elements be rationally designed and rapidly synthesized to achieve high catalytic efficiency and durability for ammonia decomposition?
item.material_system: RuRhCoNi (Ru-4 MEA-NPs) and RuRhCoNiIr (Ru-5 MEA-NPs) nanoparticles; precursor elements: Ru, Rh, Co, Ni, Ir, Pd, Cr, Fe, Cu, Mo
item.processing_route: Rapid high-temperature synthesis via electrical Joule heating: multi-elemental salt precursors (0.05 M in ethanol) deposited on activated carbon nanofibers, heated to 1500 K for 500 ms (0.5 s), followed by quenching
item.test_conditions: Catalytic NH3 decomposition in a fixed-bed flow reactor at atmospheric pressure; gas hourly space velocity (GHSV) ≥30,000; reaction temperatures stepped from 300°C to 550°C; in situ stability testing in electron microscope up to 873 K for 30 min per point
key_findings: Ru-4 MEA-NPs reached 100% NH3 decomposition at ~470°C, whereas a pure Ru sample with similar loading showed only 30% conversion.
MEA-NPs exhibited an ultrasmall and uniform particle size distribution of ~3 to 5 nm.
Ru atoms in Ru-5 MEA-NPs diffuse approximately 100 times slower than in a binary Ru-Ni alloy, indicating sluggish diffusion.
The Ru-5 MEA-NPs maintained a homogeneous alloy structure and uniform dispersion after in situ annealing up to 873 K.
Ru-5 MEA-NPs outperformed a Ru-5 sample prepared by impregnation (annealed at 300°C for 1 hour), confirming the alloy structure's role in performance.
The alloy formation temperature for Ru-Ni bimetallic is ~2000 K, while it decreases to 871 K for Ru-4 and 584 K for Ru-5 MEA-NPs due to entropy effects.
MEA-NPs showed a fragmented domain structure with rich interfaces, unlike the single domain structure of pure Ru NPs.
item.mechanism: Entropy-driven thermodynamic stabilization (increased mixing entropy lowers Gibbs free energy) combined with kinetic stabilization (sluggish diffusion caused by lattice distortion and atomic size mismatch) prevents phase separation and elemental segregation, enabling the formation of uniform alloy structures from immiscible elements.
item.limitations: DFT calculations did not account for vibrational energy and surface-energy effects in nanoparticles, meaning predicted formation temperatures represent a thermodynamic lower limit; short-range chemical ordering exists, meaning the alloy is not completely random.
item.future_work: The computationally aided rational design and rapid synthesis method can be generally used to accelerate catalyst discovery in multi-elemental materials for various catalytic reactions.
quotes: We report the computationally aided, entropy-driven design and synthesis of highly efficient and durable catalyst MEA-NPs.
The mixing enthalpy (ΔHmix) acts as the barrier to alloy formation, but the entropy-driven effect (−T*ΔSmix) favors an alloy phase, particularly at high temperatures.
The outstanding performance of the MEA-NPs is likely a synergistic effect from the ultrafine size of the NPs (3 to 5 nm), their multi-elemental composition, and their homogeneous alloy structure.
